description:
Found by the round s543s (the companion `--all --quick` on MAIN-READY-108 4a0fd0ec): perl's t/op/attrproto.t row 39 "Sanity checking that eval of anonymous sub didn't croak" (t-line 104) is a NEW failing row; one-file runs and probes put the move at s543h (MAIN-READY-107 0eb941e3, string-eval name resolution: the block-package requalifier).

Reproducer (perl 5.40.3 vs PCL; the archive extractions of the merge shas in ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s543/round2/trees/, probes in the s543s worktree scratch/s543s/probes/attrproto{,2,3,4}.pl):

    no warnings;
    my $r = eval 'package Q; my $a = sub(bar) {}; 1;';
    print defined $r ? "ok\n" : "DIES: $@";

perl: ok.  MR-106 (b58114ca): ok.  MR-107 (0eb941e3) and MR-108 (4a0fd0ec): DIES: PCL internal: the binder holds no record of $a in `(bar)` at line 1 (no-token) -- the block-package requalifier cannot home it at (eval 1) line 1.

What triggers it (main 4a0fd0ec):
- dies: `package Q; my $a = sub(bar) {}`, `my $b = sub(bar) {}`, `my $a; $a = sub(bar) {}`, `{ my $a = sub(bar) {}; }`, `my ($a) = sub(bar) {}`, and the test's own `my $a = sub(bar) : prototype(baz) {}` -- all after `package Q;` inside the eval text;
- works: `my $x = sub(bar) {}` (another name), `my $a = sub($) { 7 }` (a prototype of sigils), `my $a = sub {}`, the same text WITHOUT the leading `package Q;`, `my $a = 1`.
So the shape is: a lexical named like a sort variable ($a / $b) + an anonymous sub whose prototype text contains a word, in a package-switching eval text -- the requalifier offers `$a` to the binder at the prototype's token.  A prototype with letters is legal perl (it warns "Illegal character in prototype" under warnings); the case is rare outside perl's own tests, but the failure is an internal error, not perl's behaviour.

Bar for the fix: perl's t/op/attrproto.t row 39 passes again (one-file: MR-106 24/24 -> MR-107 23/25), the probe above prints ok, and a Pl/t row guards it.
=== WIDER THAN FILED (the reviewing session, 2026-11-24; probes ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s543/review/probes-1124/ t.pl e.pl f2.pl, perl -> MR-106 -> MR-107 -> main) ===
1. It is NOT about `$a` / `$b`: ANY variable whose bare name is a SUBSTRING of the prototype's text is offered at the Prototype token -- `eval 'package Q; my $r = sub(bar) {}; 1'` and `my $ba = sub(bar) {}` die the same ("no record of $r in `(bar)`", "no record of $ba"); `my $x = sub(bar) {}` (no `x` in `bar`) is right.  So the candidate test matches the name against the token's TEXT.
2. THE FILE-LEVEL FACE IS OLDER THAN s543h: `{ package Q; my $r = sub(bar) {}; print "ok\n"; }` is `Transpile failed: PCL internal: the binder holds no record of $r in `(bar)` ...` on MR-106, MR-107 and main alike (perl: ok).  s543h did not create the defect; it sent eval text through the same requalifier, which is the companion row's move.
3. A SIGNATURE is a Prototype token to PPI, and there the shape is legal perl with no warning: `eval q{package Q; use feature 'signatures'; sub nm ($a, $b = $a) { $a + $b } nm(4)}` dies "no record of $a in `($a, $b = $a)`" (perl 8).  With other names it is right (`sub n1 ($x, $y = $x)`, an anonymous sub's signature, `($self, %o)`), and the file-level block forms `{ package Q; sub n1 ($x, $y = $x) {...} }` / `package Q { ... }` are right: the `$a` / `$b` face needs the eval region's `$a`-`$b` keep rule.
FIX DIRECTION: the candidate generator of `_rewrite_var_uses` must not offer a Prototype / Signature token by its text -- a prototype of sigils names no variable, and a signature's variables are the BINDER's parameters (their declarations) and its default expressions' uses, which the binder already records token by token.  ONE place (rule 11): find where the token set for a canon is built and what it does with `PPI::Token::Prototype`; do not add a skip at the die.  Guard rows: the three faces above + the breaking shape -- a signature DEFAULT that reads a package variable of the region (`package Q; our $d = 3; sub n ($x, $y = $d) { $x + $y }` in an eval text and in a file-level block, with `$d` an `our` of ANOTHER package too) must still be requalified.
Found beside it and filed separately: #5374 (a `my` after the text's own `our` in an eval text behind `package`).

=== s543s NOTE (2026-11-24, the round's FULL companion run on MAIN-READY-110 26d0dac4; Opus 5.5) -- the EVAL faces pass on -110, the FILE-LEVEL face does not ===
The full run (round2/comp-full-all.log) reads op/attrproto.t 24/24 again: row 39 is a FIXED ROW and left baselines/perl-suite-fails.tsv by edit (no baseline row is keyed on this task now).  One-file runs (round2/specs/comp2.log): MR-108 4a0fd0ec 23/25, MR-109 cbcc9165 23/25, MR-110 24/24 -- moved by s543k (which member: not bisected).  Probes (~/pcl-agent-scratch/s543/round2/declrefs/p5310b.pl, p5310c.pl), perl -> MR-109 -> MR-110:
    eval 'package Q; my $a = sub(bar) {}; 1'                                    perl 1 | MR-109 DIES "no record of $a in `(bar)`" | MR-110 1
    eval 'package Q; my $r = sub(bar) {}; 1'                                    perl 1 | MR-109 DIES                               | MR-110 1
    eval 'package Q; my $a = sub(bar) : prototype(baz) {}; 1'                   perl 1 | MR-109 DIES                               | MR-110 1
    eval q{package Q; use feature 'signatures'; sub nm ($a, $b = $a) {...} nm(4)}  perl 8 | MR-109 DIES                           | MR-110 8
    eval q{package Q; our $d = 3; ... sub n ($x, $y = $d) { $x + $y } n(1)}     perl 4 | MR-110 4 (the breaking shape: still requalified)
    { package Q; my $r = sub(bar) {}; print "ok file-level\n"; }   (a FILE)     perl ok | MR-108 and MR-110: "Transpile failed: PCL internal: the binder holds no record of $r in `(bar)` ... the block-package requalifier cannot home it"
So what is left of this task on MAIN-READY-110 is face 2 of the reviewing session's note (the file-level block); the eval faces and the companion row are fixed.  Not closed by the round (the file-level face is live; a guard row for the eval faces is the fix batch's).
